A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we provide a new security definition that captures the intuitive notion of fairness, and that enjoys strong composition properties, in a model that captures the fact that the parties may need additional resources to handle malicious behavior.

we have a new notion of security for cryptographic protocols, which is similar to the UC notion of security, but allows for aborts, and which is also more general and composable than previous notions that allow for aborts.
we introduce a new security model for cryptographic protocols, called resource fairness, and show that it is both necessary and sufficient for the security of protocols in the UC framework.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the standard simulation paradigm can indeed be used to define and prove security of cryptographic protocols in the presence of resource-bounded adversaries.
resource fairness and composability of protocols can be achieved simultaneously.
, in the context of resource fairness, we can prove strong composition theorems for protocols that are not necessarily UC secure.
